title: Messages counted with an invalid counter, through streaming, fingerprints and #55 joins
matrix: input, output, cache-read and cache-write breakdowns
policy: P8 with P2 and P4: a message stays flawed once any of its records had an invalid counter, through streamed growth and when its partial groups join a pair (#55), so neither a later valid copy nor a relaunch makes it exact. Flaws are counted per identity group, like identity.
derivation: s1: P (msg_41a + req_41a) [100, output "?" left out], then [100, 40]: growth +40, still flawed. N (no ids) [7, output -1 left out]: fingerprinted, flawed. M (msg_41m only) [50, "x" left out]: incomplete, flawed. Q1 (msg_41q only) [9, 1]: incomplete. Q2 (req_41q only) [9, 1, read -3 left out]: incomplete, flawed. Step 1: input 100+7+50+9+9 = 175, output 40+1+1 = 42, 5 calls = 217; identified 1, incomplete 3, fingerprinted 1; flawed P N M Q2 = 4. s2: the pair msg_41m + req_41m takes over M, keeping its flaw, and adds output 5. The pair msg_41q + req_41q takes over Q1 and merges Q2: Q2 is taken back with its flaw and counted again into the pair, adding no tokens but the flaw; then output +1. Step 2: input 100+7+50+9 = 166, output 40+5+2 = 47, 4 calls = 213; identified 1, incomplete 2, fingerprinted 1; flawed 4. Read in the other file order the pairs count first and the partials join them, adding no growth but their flaws: the same.
